newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Aramco receives gas oil/jet term bids - trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Aramco receives gas oil/jet term bids - trade.

text.p: Potential term lifters of middle distillates from state-owned Saudi Aramco have submitted their opening proposals on volume and pricing for cargo liftings in 1997, oil traders based in the Gulf said on Monday.
"The bid deadline for gas oil and jet was today. We will probably hear back from Aramco in a month," one trader said.

Traders said their initial pricing position was based in line with India Oil Corp's 1997 term contract with Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) which was agreed at a premium of around 70 cents for one percent sulphur gas oil and 55 cents for jet.
Aramco has not indicated how much gas oil or jet-kerosene is available though most cargoes will be exported from the Red Sea and supplies will fluctuate on a quarterly basis.
"The first quarter and fourth quarter is preferred (for lifters)," one trader said.

Rising domestic middle distillate consumption has capped Aramco's gas oil exports in recent years though the partial removal of state price subsidies on local petroleum products last year has freed up export quantities.
